Cyber Attack Hits Jordan’s Gas & Water Utilities Sector, Disrupting Operations

AMMAN, June 12—A major cyber attack targeting firms in Jordan’s Gas & Water Utilities industry is disrupting services and prompting emergency measures, company officials and union representatives said Wednesday.

The incident, which began late Tuesday, appears to involve ransomware affecting the IT systems of several companies, including Jordan Valley Gas and Petra Water Services. Industry sources said attackers encrypted key operational and administrative files, preventing staff from accessing billing, maintenance scheduling, and remote monitoring platforms.

“We detected unusual activity on our network and immediately initiated shutdown protocols to contain the spread,” said Mohammad Al-Rashid, spokesperson for Jordan Valley Gas. “Our teams are working around the clock to restore critical functions, but at this stage, many of our digital systems remain offline.”

According to the Jordan Utilities Workers Union, employees at multiple sites have been instructed to revert to manual processes where possible. “Field teams are using paper logs to track deliveries and maintenance,” said union leader Fatin Mahameed. “It’s a challenging situation, as many tasks now take significantly longer and require more coordination.”

Several water treatment plants operated by Petra Water Services are also impacted. “We are prioritizing essential operations to maintain service continuity, but some non-urgent maintenance and administrative work is delayed,” said a company statement.

The Jordanian Cyber Defense Authority said it is working with affected firms to investigate the breach. While no timeline has been given for full restoration, officials cautioned that recovery could take days.

Local industry analyst Khaled Samara said the incident highlights the sector’s reliance on digital infrastructure. “Gas and water utilities in Jordan have invested heavily in automation over the last decade. This attack exposes vulnerabilities that need urgent attention,” he said.

At the time of writing, the attack is ongoing and firms across the industry remain on high alert. Security experts have urged all sector companies to review cyber defenses and enhance staff awareness.
